content: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a great deal of it.
author: Seneca
sourceWork: De Brevitate Vitae (On the Shortness of Life)
story:
We constantly complain that life is too short, yet we squander our hours as if we had an infinite supply stored in a bank. Seneca observed people agonizing over every penny in their wallet, while casually giving away their irreplaceable time to boring obligations, petty feuds, and endless distractions.

Life is plenty long enough to accomplish meaningful, beautiful things if it is properly invested. It only feels brief because we treat our time like it has no value until it is almost gone.
reflectionPrompt: If you looked candidly at how you spent the last 48 hours, how much of that precious time went toward things that hold zero lasting value?
